title: Quarterly orchestration: Dedicated capacity burst-policy lattice and canary calendar
creator: Priya Patel
description: Scope: Define and deliver a policy lattice and rollout calendar for per-customer burst windows, fairshare corridors, and canary orchestration for Dedicated GPU pools. This ticket coordinates PM, Eng, Infra, and Finance to produce a repeatable quarterly roadmap slice that reduces overcommit oscillation, limits unexpected egress to burst reserves, and provides deterministic cost guardrails for customers on reserved capacity.
context: Background: We ran three ad-hoc capacity incidents last quarter where aggressive burst requests caused reservoir depletion and cross-tenant latency regressions. Current controls are per-pool thresholds and emergency throttles; customers have requested predictable burst windows and clearer billing behavior. Finance needs a guardrail model to estimate marginal cost for burst usage before committing to larger reserved SKUs.
objectives: Ship a documented policy lattice that combines: base reservation quota, scheduled burst windows, on-demand fairshare, and emergency fallback tiers
Deliver a canary calendar and automated test harness to validate lattice behavior across traffic patterns (steady, spiky, diurnal)
Provide a unit-cost model and dashboard prototype that estimates per-customer marginal cost when bursting into reservoir capacity
Reduce unplanned reservoir drains by 60% in controlled canaries and cut cross-tenant latency regressions during peak bursts
success_metrics: Reservoir drain events reduced by 60% in pilot pools over 6 weeks
95th percentile tail latency during burst tests remains within 1.3x baseline
Dashboard shows forecasted marginal cost error <10% vs simulated bill run
Customer-facing burst SLA language and runbook approved by compliance/finance
milestones: 2026-04-01: Finalize policy lattice spec (quota + scheduled bursts + fairshare) and sign off with Eng & Legal
2026-04-15: Deliver simulation harness and initial spike matrix (low/med/high/concurrent)
2026-05-01: Canary pilot in Pool-EU-2 with 3 beta customers; automated rollback and telemetry hooks enabled
2026-05-25: Run canary stress week; collect SLO/ledger data and iterate on cost model
2026-06-10: Dashboard alpha for Finance & CS; policy language for customer docs
2026-06-25: Final runbook, release notes, and handoff to Ops for broader rollout
planned_tasks: Write policy lattice spec and decision matrix for competing goals (latency vs cost vs fairness)
Implement simulation harness based on historical request traces and synthetic spikes
Add telemetry tags to request router to attribute reservoir consumption to customer and route policy decisions
Prototype dashboard: forecasted marginal cost and burst corridor utilization
Coordinate legal/finance review for billing language and SLA adjustments
Prepare canary checklist, rollback criteria, and incident playbooks
risks: Policy complexity leads to unexpected customer UX regressions unless surfaced simply in Console
Simulation mismatch with production patterns (edge cases: multi-region fans and KV-cache hotwarm effects)
Finance projection uncertainty if burst pricing assumptions are inaccurate
mitigations: Include design discipline: 2 CTA-level UX language variants and validate with 5 customers
Run shadow traffic for 48 hours prior to canary enabling to validate simulation fidelity
Conservative cost model with margin of safety and explicit assumptions doc for Finance
